tonight.headline: JuiceJam are starting a ruled-out receiver. Nothing for you to change
body: Tucker Kraft's 6.6 from Thursday is all JuiceJam have. ESPN projects you 119.6 to their 112.0, a 54% chance. Your lineup as set is the projection lineup, and none of your starters is questionable.
Golden scored 21.0 on your bench on Thursday. That was the projection's call and it was the right process; it doesn't move next week.

case.label: The Collins hole
case.body: Nico Collins is OUT for Houston (Colts/Texans report via Yahoo; CBS) and still in JuiceJam's WR slot, with Jameson Williams (11.0) on their bench. If they don't fix it, that's a zero.

case.label: Their backs

case.label: What would change it
case.body: JuiceJam swap Williams in for Collins before 11:00, which takes roughly 11 points off your margin.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Conditional. Only when rosters unlock, only if the Week 3 archive trips Lloyd's clause, only if Downs is still a free agent
doFirst.title: If Lloyd's clause trips: drop him, add Josh Downs
doFirst.subtitle: Not armed today. Lloyd is locked and his thesis hasn't formally closed. Never spend waiver priority on this.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Lloyd was held as Green Bay's lead back with Jacobs away. Thursday he was the RB3: 15 snaps to Brooks's 26 and Johnson's 22 (Acme Packing Co.), 3.8 points. His written falsifier is Brooks or Johnson out-touching him two weeks running. Week 2 was a tie on touches (8 each, archive), so it hasn't fired yet. If the Week 3 archive shows him out-touched again, it has. He's 67.9% owned; I disagree with the market because the snap order, not the box score, says he's third.

case.label: The add
case.body: Josh Downs: the waiver tool has him RISING (6 then 13.5 opportunities). The role reason is Alec Pierce on IR (heel) for at least four weeks, with Ashton Dulin also out; Downs drew 9 targets once Pierce left in Week 2 (NBC). Free agent here, so no priority.

case.label: The price
case.body: If Downs has moved to waivers when rosters unlock, stop. IPADE priority never resets and a WR4 is not a starter-level need.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: The archive shows Lloyd leading Green Bay's backs in touches on Thursday, or Jacobs is reinstated. Either keeps him. For Downs: under five targets against Houston with Pierce and Dulin out would say the role isn't his.

case.body: Brooks 26 snaps, Johnson 22, Lloyd 15 (Acme Packing Co.); PFF call it a three-way split no one should start. 3.8 points.

case.label: The fix
case.body: The card above: a conditional drop once rosters unlock, if the archive confirms the clause.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: The Week 3 archive showing Lloyd with the most touches despite fewer snaps.

trades.theirGainLine: Their gain is +1.7 this week: Tuten (11.0) replaces Rachaad White (9.3) in their second RB slot, and Lamar scores them nothing behind Josh Allen.

case.label: Their surplus
case.body: Lamar sits at slot 20 behind Josh Allen at slot 0 in a one-quarterback league (league file, checked this run). He is not on Baltimore's report (CBS).

case.label: Your gain
case.body: Lamar 20.1 over Lawrence 16.4 this week, +3.7. On season projections Lamar 297.3 to Tuten 166.9.

case.label: Honest risk
case.body: On raw season totals it reads lopsided in your favour, which is why it's a longshot. Their weekly gain is real but small, and Barkley is healthy, so Tuten has no starting role for you to lose.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Team 13 start a second real back over White, drop or trade a quarterback, or Lamar lands on a Baltimore report. Don't re-send; answer only if they open the conversation.

trades.copyText: Hi — would you do Lamar for Bhayshul Tuten? Lamar can't start for you behind Allen, and Tuten (11.0 this week) would start over White for you. Your gain is bigger this week than mine.
